articles.title: git stash Is Shared Across Worktrees. Two Parallel Agents Popped Each Other's Work
articles.excerpt: Book: Prompt Engineering Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for develope…
articles.body: Book: Prompt Engineering Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub Two coding agents were working on one repository at the same time, each in its own git worktree, each on its own issue. Both ran the same check: stash the fix, run the tests to prove they fail without it, pop the fix back. Agent A's pop brought back agent B's stash. B's pop brought back A's. Each worktree now held a file from the other task, and the stash list was empty. That is the report in objectstack issue #5742 , opened on August 6, 2026.

articles.title: BookLore has 814 exact title matches and no application fingerprint; inventory the library, then verify identity
articles.excerpt: BookLore has 814 exact title matches and no application fingerprint; inventory the library, then verify identity BookLore is a self-hosted, multi-user digital library with local and OIDC authenticatio…
articles.body: BookLore has 814 exact title matches and no application fingerprint; inventory the library, then verify identity BookLore is a self-hosted, multi-user digital library with local and OIDC authentication, book folders, metadata enrichment and OPDS access. Its first-run flow creates an administrator account, then the administrator creates libraries and adds users. That makes the application a good example of why a precise title count can be useful even when an app fingerprint is absent. On 2026-11-05, a count-only ZoomEye query with sub_type=all , page 1 and page size 1 returned 814 matches for title=="BookLore" and zero for app="BookLore" .

Technical Impact and Risks For developers and system administrators, this breach is particularly concerning due to the nature of the exposed data: FTP/SFTP Credentials: These are primary vectors for site management. With these credentials, an attacker can modify source code, inject malicious scripts (such as credit card skimmers or malware), or delete entire directories.

articles.title: When a node loses its lease anyway: a takeover, second by second
articles.excerpt: I am building a cloud trade copier for MetaTrader. Each follower account has one broker session on one node, and that node copies the master's trades onto it. In an earlier post I described how a node…
articles.body: I am building a cloud trade copier for MetaTrader. Each follower account has one broker session on one node, and that node copies the master's trades onto it. In an earlier post I described how a node leases its accounts from Postgres: a node_id and a lease_until on the account row, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to claim, and a node that stops sending orders 15 seconds before its lease ends. That post was about keeping ownership. This one is about losing it: what happens, second by second, when a node is cut off from the database, another node takes its accounts, and both have to end up agreeing with what is actually open at the broker.

articles.title: Open Source AI Is Booming. The Money Is in Everything Around the Model.
articles.excerpt: The model is free. The bill isn't — and that's the whole open-source AI business model. Everyone keeps announcing "open" models like the download is the product. It isn't. The weights are free; everyt…
articles.body: The model is free. The bill isn't — and that's the whole open-source AI business model. Everyone keeps announcing "open" models like the download is the product. It isn't. The weights are free; everything that turns a download into something a real company can actually run is where the money changes hands. If you're still arguing about which model is "most open," you're missing the only question that matters: who gets paid, and for what? "Open" mostly means open-weight, not open-source. You get the weights, not the training data, not the recipe, not reproducibility. Several of the biggest "open" models carry custom licences with revenue thresholds for managed services. Read the licence file, not the marketing page — the marketing will cost you later.

articles.excerpt: How "Forrest Gump", pizza, and a massive supporting cast of furballs came together to make one of "Star Trek"'s finest hours.
articles.body: When "Star Trek" celebrated its 60th anniversary in September, it was a strangely muted affair. Sure, there were fan events, screenings, and even an attempt at a world record for the biggest simultaneous Vulcan salute in history , but the lack of a "Doctor Who"-style birthday episode felt like a glaring omission. It was like everyone had shown up for the party, but the organizers had forgotten to book the headline entertainment. Luckily, there were rather more fireworks for the show's 30th birthday, when both "Voyager" and "Deep Space Nine" marked the occasion in style. "Voyager" episode "Flashback" took Tuvok (Tim Russ) back to his days on the USS Excelsior bridge alongside Original Series vets Hikaru Sulu (George Takei) and Janice Rand (Grace Lee Whitney).

articles.title: NASA's Swift space telescope crashes back to Earth after failed rescue attempt
articles.excerpt: NASA's Swift space telescope crashed back to Earth today (Nov. 4), three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost the observatory to a higher orbit.
articles.body: NASA's Swift space telescope has reached the end of its long and winding road. Swift fell uncontrolled to Earth today (Nov. 4), 22 years after it launched but just three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost it to a higher, life-extending orbit. The 3,200-pound (1,450 kilograms) observatory reentered Earth's atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 GMT) today over northern Sumatra, according to satellite tracker Jonathan McDowell , who cited U.S. Space Force data. The fall likely didn't make much of an impact; NASA officials predicted beforehand that most of the minibus-sized Swift would burn up as it fell, and they put the odds of any of the surviving pieces hurting anyone on Earth at just 1 in 2,100.

articles.title: Mars isn't dead — recent volcanic activity reveals it's just sleeping
articles.excerpt: Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead" but new spacecraft observations suggests the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping.
articles.body: Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead," but new spacecraft observations suggest the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping. That means that Olympus Mons , the extinct Martian volcano that at around 16 miles (26 kilometers) above the surrounding Martian plains is the largest mountain in the solar system , may in fact be a slumbering giant. The observations were made with the European Space Agency (ESA) mission ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) as it studied volcanic fissures along the Alba Mons region of the Red Planet. Alba Mons is in the Tharsis region of Mars, the same area that is home to Olympus Mons.
